_comment: P6 Claude fleet controller policy. ENFORCE requires approved_enforce_digest to equal FleetPolicy.digest() AND an --allow-enforce invocation flag. Flipped to enforce under Diego's explicit cutover approval on 2026-09-01; the reaper was retired in the same change (and stayed retired -- see hermes commits b7348d08/dc35ee74 for a brief re-enable and its revert). 2026-09-01 ~19:2xZ: fleet_min_roots lowered 30 -> 25 on Diego's explicit instruction, and approved_enforce_digest RE-APPROVED in the same edit to the new policy digest -- changing any policy field changes digest(), and leaving the old digest would silently demote the controller to shadow on the next pass. To roll back: set mode to shadow OR null approved_enforce_digest (either disarms enforcement on the next pass).
_comment_d7_max_age: 2026-09-02, on Diego's explicit instruction ('do P1 too'): d7_max_age_seconds 360 -> 1200, approved_enforce_digest RE-APPROVED in the same edit (549c9ed1... -> 27ac9af1...). NOTE policy_version is ITSELF a digest input, so bumping it to p6-2026-09-02-1 moved the digest a second time -- re-approving on the d7 change alone would have left a stale pin and silently demoted the lane. Never hand-write this value: derive it with load_policy(config).digest(), which is what test_tracked_config_enforce_is_coherently_pinned now asserts. WHY: the binding constraint is the PRODUCER's re-ping interval, not the task cadence. ResourcePressureMonitor emits at most once per re_alert_cooldown_seconds (900s) while an episode is merely sustained, so the newest event's age at an arbitrary pass ranges over [0, 900). A 360s freshness window therefore read 'stale' through roughly 60% of any live episode -- structurally, at ANY pass cadence. 1200s clears 900s with 300s of margin. SHORTENING THE TASK WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED THIS: the cadence is PT10M by Diego's own deliberate 2026-09-01 change (hermes 776c3eb3f, for PT-limit headroom under load), and no cadence beats a 900s producer interval. COST, stated plainly: the monitor emits NOTHING when pressure clears (resource_monitor: 'if not reasons: return None'), so staleness is the ONLY thing that disarms after an episode ends -- this widens the post-episode authorization window from 6 to 20 minutes. Bounded in practice by the chronically-latched disk axis, whose 900s re-ping carries a corrected axes_latched set within ~15 min of a true clear, and by the unchanged two-strike + 30-min-idle + 1800s-cooldown + 1-tree-per-pass gates. The clean fix that would let this come back down is an explicit episode-cleared emission; not built, see loops reaper-retirement-commit-gap-20260901.
_comment_commit_pct_arm: 2026-09-02, P2, on Diego's explicit instruction ('do P2'): commit_pct_arm added at 90.0 -- a SECOND arming axis, ORed with spawn_latency, never ANDed. approved_enforce_digest RE-APPROVED in the same edit. WHY 90 AND NOT THE RETIRED REAPER'S 85: 85.0 is resource_monitor's own DEFAULT_COMMIT_PCT_THRESHOLD, i.e. where ALERTING fires and where the historical cascade merely BEGINS; the documented crash-loop band (agent memory gateway_crashloop_commit_exhaustion.md, mempalace_zombie_watchdog_recovery.md) is 89-94%. 90 acts inside the cascade and leaves 85-90 to alerting. It deliberately does NOT align with COMMIT_BANDS' 'severe' edge (92.0), which would miss the documented 89-91 onset. CERTIFIED DIFFERENTLY FROM SPAWN, on purpose: spawn arms off the axis set alone and so survives the producer's hysteresis band, while commit additionally requires the event's LIVE commit_pct >= 90 -- the axis latches at 85, so a latched-but-recovering commit axis must not keep a kill authorized on a flag. NO LONGER UNCOVERED as of P5 below (2026-09-02) -- this comment used to end 'STILL NOT COVERED: triggers_armed continues to AND this with the fleet-size half ... Diego's to settle', and Diego settled it. See _comment_commit_bypass. Set to null to turn the axis off (and re-approve the digest).
_comment_commit_bypass: 2026-09-02, P5, on Diego's explicit instruction ('do 1 and 5') after the fleet-min-roots morning briefing: commit_bypass_min_roots added at 2. This closes the gap the P2 comment and planner.evaluate_pressure both flagged as NOT COVERED and as Diego's to settle -- triggers_armed ANDs pressure with the fleet-size half, so a box deep in the 89-94% crash-loop band got NO relief from the commit axis whenever its root count sat at or below fleet_min_roots. When the commit axis is among the axes that ACTUALLY ARMED a pass, the fleet-size floor now drops from fleet_min_roots (25) to this value. approved_enforce_digest RE-APPROVED in the same edit and policy_version bumped to p6-2026-09-02-3; the digest was DERIVED with load_policy(config).digest(), never hand-written. WHY 2 AND NOT 0: a floor of 0 authorizes killing the last remaining tree, which on this box is routinely the session doing the diagnosing; 2 means the lane acts from 3 trees up. WHY KEYED ON armed_axes AND NOT ON commit_high BEING LATCHED: the commit axis is certified on a LIVE commit_pct >= commit_pct_arm (90), so a recovering box loses the bypass on the same pass it loses the arming rather than a hysteresis band later. It can only ever LOWER the floor (min() is taken), so a value above fleet_min_roots is inert, not a back door. WHAT STILL BOUNDS IT, unchanged: max_trees_per_pass 1, strikes_required 2 within strike_max_age_seconds 900, idle_min_minutes 30, cooldown_seconds 1800 -- so the widened authorization buys at most one idle-30min tree per 30 minutes, and only while commit is live at or past 90. Set to null to turn the bypass off (and re-approve the digest).
